messages:
Anna (product): thinking about a controlled 'escape hatch' for customers who hit tier limits during critical surges — goal: keep apps alive without opening the floodgates :thinking_face:
Matt (sales): +1 from field. Customers keep asking for a temporary bypass for launches. needs to be low fric for them but safe for us
Jess (legal): we need clear guardrails. any automated bypass should be auditable and time-limited. also must appear in contract as an exception process
Omar (infra): depends on how we route capacity. quick option is a short-lived 'burst token' that temporarily bumps quota and routes to burst pool. we can enforce TTL and telemetry
Rita (finance): must tie to billing/commit model. if we let auto-burst, it should either convert to paid overage or consume prepaid credits. need ledger entries for reconciliation
Anna (product): rough proposal: two modes — automatic soft-burst (up to X tokens, 10min) for all tiers; manual approved burst (sales/finance ok) for larger windows. automatic should have strict frequency limits
Matt (sales): agree. auto-burst for dev/launch events is huge for PLG teams. manual approval path for enterprise needing longer runway
Jess (legal): require customer opt-in for auto-burst in TOS or onboarding checkbox. manual bursts -> amend SOW or email approval recorded in audit trail
Omar (infra): implementation sketch:
```
if customer.burst_opt_in and usage.spike < SOFT_BURST_LIMIT:
  grant_burst(ttl=600s)
  log("auto-burst granted")
else:
  create_manual_request(ticket)
```
We can add rate-limits per customer and per org to avoid abuse
Rita (finance): what are SOFT_BURST_LIMIT numbers? need to model P95/P99 cost impact. can we simulate cost delta for typical spikes?
Anna (product): propose soft burst = 200k tokens per 10min window for Starter/Scale, 1M tokens per 10min for Enterprise evaluation. open to revision after cost sims
Matt (sales): can we add a 'burst credit' bundle customers can buy — like prepaid burst tokens? customers prefer predictable options
Jess (legal): for prepaid burst credits, contract language simpler. also require expiry window (e.g., 12 months) and non-refundable clause
Omar (infra): telemetry hooks we need: burst origin (auto/manual), trigger metric, TTL, routing path, model variant used, latency/queue impact. prod console surface should show active bursts and who approved
Anna (product): launch gating checklist draft:
- docs: UX & onboarding text for opt-in
- backend: TTL, rate-limits, audit log, billing ledger
- product: burst SKU + UI for purchase
- legal: contract addendum language
- finance: pricing model + cost simulations
- infra: console visibility + guardrails
- support: runbook for manual approvals
If any of these not covered, we don't GA
Rita (finance): timeline: I can run cost sims this week if Omar provides sample traces. need 3 cost scenarios (optimistic/median/worst)
Omar (infra): will export spike traces from last 6 months. attaching sample soon — deploy-bot will post when available :robot_face:
deploy-bot: attached: s3://redwood-spike-traces/2026-q1-sample.json.gz
Matt (sales): for prioritization — recommend feature flagged rollout to a small set of customers (5 pilot orgs) and reserved capacity on Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor issues
Jess (legal): pilot customers should sign a short pilot agreement that clarifies limits and billing for bursts
Anna (product): next steps: (1) Omar & Rita run sims + telemetry export, (2) Jess drafts pilot agreement language, (3) Product builds spec for auto/manual flows and UX, (4) pick pilot customers. I'll own coordinating. tagging @Matt for customer shortlist
Matt (sales): I'll send 6 candidates by EOD and mark which prefer prepaid vs manual
Anna (product): perfect. quick question — what metric should we use to auto-grant? short window QPS vs token-rate?
Omar (infra): token-rate + steep derivative (dT/dt) — e.g., tokens/min increasing > 3x baseline over last 5m and under absolute cap. avoids noisy small bursts
Rita (finance): once sims are in, I want a table: tier | soft_limit | cost_per_burst | recommended_price (prepaid). will loop legal if pricing impacts contracts
Jess (legal): flag — any auto-bursts that materially change customer invoice must be consented in onboarding. small auto-bursts ok if covered by prepaid or TOS checkbox
Anna (product): good call. I'll draft onboarding checkbox copy: "Allow Redwood to temporarily extend quota for short, occasional spikes. Charges may apply." short and clear
Matt (sales): :thumbsup: customers will love a predictable prepaid option
Anna (product): OK — I'll collate notes into a spec doc and post here when ready. aim to have pilot-ready checklist next Wed
Omar (infra): sending traces in ~2h
Rita (finance): will review sims on Thurs
Jess (legal): will draft pilot contract by Fri
Anna (product): thanks team — this feels actionable. closing the loop once spec is up :white_check_mark:
